root_cause: to_csv_rows in utils.py was declared with headers: List[str] = []. Python evaluates default argument expressions exactly once at function-definition time, so every call that omits headers shares the same list object. Any code that obtained a reference to that shared default and mutated it (via extend, append, or +=) would corrupt all subsequent headerless calls, which would then receive the already-mutated list instead of the canonical six-column default. The fix is to use headers: Optional[List[str]] = None and guard internally with `row_headers = headers if headers is not None else default_headers`.

items.reason: This is the bug site; the mutable default list is shared across all callers, making the function's output silently depend on call-site mutation history.
Calls to_csv_rows(expenses) with no headers argument; if the shared default is mutated by another caller earlier in the process, export_csv silently produces a wrong header row in the output file.
Calls export_csv which calls to_csv_rows without headers; inherits the corruption risk from export_csv and exposes it to every consumer of the API.

CLI entry point that calls export_to_csv; a corrupted header would silently appear in the output CSV file with no error raised, but cmd_export has no direct interaction with the default list object itself.
